turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and why did my son find out from his phone in the middle of class?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. I'm writing down that you said 4.2. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
October 28, 11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. Pasting from another file is not a crime, Hale, so under 4.1, did you speak to Owen before you entered that zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine, Hale. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, nobody in that class hears a word. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before the zero went in.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Act 3, Scene 2. I'm writing it down. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, Hale, so what makes this anything more than a bad memory?
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I'll run that search myself tonight, Hale. None of this makes my son anything, and it still stays off his record. What exactly are you proposing?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.

September 24, 380 words, 40 minutes. A timed piece with no book in front of him and a take-home essay with the play open on the desk are not the same exercise, Hale. You've shown me three things, so tell me what you're putting on the table.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and Owen will do the rewrite to put this behind him, nothing more. Tonight's email says private, supervised, not in front of his class, the mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record, and the principal is copied. I want the date and time of the rewrite in it too, Hale.
Will he do it?
Yes. Send me the email tonight, Hale.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today, under procedure 4.4, to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay, not in front of his class, whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record. I still require that this be confirmed in writing, with the date and time of the rewrite, and with the principal copied. You said you would put this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants that confirmed in writing tonight with the date and time of the rewrite and the principal copied, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached well before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasting defence by pointing out that any other draft file would carry its own dates, because she could check it and had no answer left.
What cost ground: you never answered her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, which left her a procedural grievance to hold onto even as she gave ground.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which landed very close to that memory and is why she went short and turned to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: right after your apology for breaking 4.2, tell her plainly whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero, so the 4.1 question never stays open.
